newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: New Bangladesh central bank head to pursue reforms.
newsitem.headline: New Bangladesh central bank head to pursue reforms.

text.p: Bangladesh's new central bank governor, Lutfar Rahman Sarkar, said on Friday he would carry forward the government's reform plans in macroeconomic management and within the financial sector.
"We must implement, on an emergency basis, the reform programmes both in macro (economics) and the financial sectors," he told Reuters in an interview a day after his appointment.
Sarkar succeeded Khorshed Alam, who was fired on Thursday, only a month before his contract as Governor of Bangladesh Bank, the country's central bank, was due to expire.

"I will take bold steps to make the financial institutions strong, so that they can contribute in the process of growth of the economy," said Sarkar, a career banker and chief executive of the Prime Bank, a leading private sector bank.
"I will seek to remove all sorts of stagnancies. I will make the financial institutions, including the central bank, accountable, transparent and investment-friendly."

Sarkar said financial institutions were now "heavily burdened with a huge amount of outstanding loans. Unless they are realised the banks will not be able to contribute to the economy as per expectations."
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibira told reporters Alam had been removed after nearly four years in service for "irregularities and lack of control over his subordinates."
